correctness.rationale: For every point of the normalized sextic affine locus, explicit composition parametrizations give the plane and a determinantal smooth cubic scroll. The identities A Q1−2h Q2=B F and 2C Q1−A Q2=D F show the two quadrics have exactly the union support; complete-intersection Cohen–Macaulayness plus generic reducedness proves radicality. On h=1 and on the unique boundary point C=1, solving the equations gives normal crossings uv=0. Adjunction and the CI Hilbert series then give stated invariants. Critical identities and finite checks reproduced by the standalone symbolic verifier; the infinite proof does not depend on test bounds.

value.rationale: The recent initiating paper explicitly distinguishes projective boundary singularities and component intersection multiplicities from its degree computations. The first nontrivial composite sextic case has two components of different degrees; an exact reduced complete-intersection ideal with a conic normal-crossing gluing is a natural, structurally complete answer to this boundary problem. The Gorenstein anticanonical identification informs geometry of the normalized reducibility locus beyond separate component enumeration. This result is more than computing an arbitrary coefficient or renaming Ritt intersections.
